newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends steady after weaker barge trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends steady after weaker barge trade.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended steady to down $1 after recovering from a weak deal in the barge market that traders said was an anomaly for an otherwise strong market.
Buying into the U.K. ahead of the government's Nov 26 budget and tight supplies of premium unleaded in northwest Europe were continuing to put a floor under prices, traders said.
In late action, Eurograde barges fell $7.50 from Friday to trade at $219.50 fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam, then offers quickly rebounded back to $226, traders said.
A buoyant U.S. market was also helping, with traders looking for arbitrage opportunities, but the focus appeared to be on Europe's own bullish fundamentals.
Barges rose to as high as $231 fob ARA after deals were concluded at $227, $228 and $230, traders said.
A slight pullback in Brent crude from its session highs also capped the gasoline rally, they said.
Unleaded regular barges held at about an $8 discount but traders said both unleaded regular and second half-November prices for premium unleaded were hard to peg.
A steeper backwardation was seen likely for the second half of the month for premium unleaded based on swaps values, but sellers said they were offering at closer to parity with prompt values.
